change.title: pr-38446-flat
change.description: Implement recovery key support for user storage providers
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Recovery codes stored in user storage are never consumed, so they can be replayed
findings.body: The recovery-code branch of isValid() returns true for any stored code (lines 326-340) without removing the used code. The local provider only burns a code in RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:105-112). UserCredentialManager.isValid (model/storage/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/UserCredentialManager.java:66-79) removes an input from toValidate as soon as the federated validator accepts it, so the local provider never runs for these codes. Result: a federated user can log in again with the same code indefinitely, allCodesUsed() never becomes true, and CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES is never re-triggered. The product code in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential hands codes to any CredentialInputUpdater, so single-use depends on each provider and nothing enforces it. Fix in this provider: remove the matched code from the stored list and write the list back, the way the local provider does. Also see the test-coverage finding on testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin.

findings.title: Regenerating codes through user storage leaves previously issued local codes valid
findings.body: When updateCredential() succeeds (line 125), the local fallback at line 129 is skipped. The fallback is the only place that deletes the existing local recovery-codes credential: RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential deletes the first stored credential of this type before creating a new one (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:39-42). If a user already has local codes (for example, from before a user-storage provider accepted this credential type), those old codes stay in the local store. RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid still checks that store (lines 99-112), and UserCredentialManager.isValid falls through to it when the storage rejects the input (model/storage/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/UserCredentialManager.java:76-79). So codes the user regenerated away still log in. Before this change, the action always went through createCredential and so removed them. Fix: delete existing stored recovery credentials on the user-storage path too, or call the local provider's delete before updateCredential.

findings.title: Raw recovery codes are sent to user storage in plaintext
findings.body: Line 119 serializes the raw generatedCodes and passes them to updateCredential(). The local path does not do this: RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues hashes each code with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/credential/RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:65-67), and the local store keeps only hashes. With this change, any external user store that accepts the type holds reversible codes that can complete a login. The test provider's isValid (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340) compares raw input, so hashing would also need the provider to hash its input. I could not find a repository decision that sets the storage format for user stores, so the author should confirm whether the plaintext is intended. Fix: pass the hashed values to the provider and hash the input when verifying.

findings.title: Recovery-code credential returned from getCredentials has no id
findings.body: updateCredential() gives the stored recovery credential an id (line 195). getCredentials() rebuilds the model with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues (lines 237-242), and createFromValues never sets an id (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/credential/RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:58-85). The OTP branch returns its stored model, which this PR now gives an id (line 179), so the two are inconsistent. The id matters: CredentialDeleteHelper.removeCredential matches federated credentials by getId() (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/requiredactions/util/CredentialDeleteHelper.java:64). A removal request for these codes therefore falls through to NotFoundException. Fix: copy the id from myUser.recoveryCodes onto the returned model.

findings.title: disableCredentialType silently ignores recovery codes, so a removal reports success while the codes still work
findings.body: supportsCredentialType(RECOVERY) now returns true (line 114). UserCredentialManager.disableCredentialType therefore calls this provider (model/storage/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/UserCredentialManager.java:175-183). This method only handles OTP (line 218). For any other type it logs 'Unsupported' (line 222) and returns, so the codes stay in place and isValid keeps accepting them. CredentialDeleteHelper then returns null after disableCredentialType (CredentialDeleteHelper.java:67-69), so the caller sees success. Today the id mismatch in the getCredentials finding makes the path fail with NotFound first. Once that id is fixed, the removal would succeed visibly while the codes still log in. Fix: either delete the recovery codes here, or make supportsCredentialType and disableCredentialType agree for this type. Confidence is medium because I did not read the account REST delete endpoint that reaches CredentialDeleteHelper.

findings.title: New recovery-code test covers only the happy path
findings.body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin logs in once with code index 0. It does not check that a used code is rejected on a second login, that a wrong code fails, that the codes run out and trigger reconfiguration, or that regeneration or removal works. A reuse assertion would have caught the replay in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340. Consider adding that case and a removal case.

findings.title: getCredentials dereferences the user entry without a null check
findings.body: getMyUser(user) (line 232) can return null if the entry was removed from the map. The new code then dereferences it (lines 235 and 247). Sibling methods guard this: getDisableableCredentialTypesStream checks myUser != null (line 259) and isConfiguredFor returns false when it is null (lines 270-271). getFederatedCredentialsStream reaches this through UserCredentialManager.java:130-146. This is in the test provider, so the effect is a test failure rather than a production one. Consider mirroring the sibling guard.

findings.title: Typo in the copied config alias
findings.body: The alias 'delayed-suthenticator-config' is misspelled. It was copied from services' RecoveryAuthnCodesAuthenticatorTest.java:137, which has the same typo. It only labels the config, so the fix is cosmetic, but it should be fixed in both places.

contracts.action: Recovery-code setup through the required action (RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.processAction stores codes)
contracts.equivalent_path: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:92-110 (createOTPCredential, the sibling that tries user storage first and falls back to the local provider)
contracts.before_after: Before: the action called the local provider's createCredential directly, which deletes any existing local recovery credential and then stores the new one. After: the helper tries user storage first. On success it never reaches the local delete, so an existing local credential stays in place.
contracts.visible_effect: The user is shown new codes and can finish the required action. The old local codes stop being shown but keep working.
contracts.failure_mode: Previously issued local recovery codes remain valid after regeneration when user storage accepts the new codes.

contracts.action: Login with a recovery code (RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.action validates via credentialManager().isValid)
contracts.before_after: Local path: the code is removed and the credential updated before success. Federated path: the storage returns true without changing its stored list, so nothing is consumed. The authenticator then reads the federated credential, sees codes remaining, and does not trigger the required action.
contracts.visible_effect: Login succeeds with the code. The same code also succeeds again on a later login.
contracts.failure_mode: Recovery codes held in user storage are replayable indefinitely.

contracts.action: Federated credentials listing via getCredentials override (feeds getFederatedCredentialsStream, which RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential uses first)
contracts.equivalent_path: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/CredentialInputUpdater.java:50-52 (the default that returns an empty stream)
contracts.before_after: Before: this provider returned no federated credentials. After: it returns a recovery credential rebuilt from the stored JSON, with no id, plus the OTP model.
contracts.visible_effect: The login form and the credential lookup see the codes. A credential listing or removal that matches by id cannot find them.
contracts.failure_mode: Removal by id fails with NotFoundException (CredentialDeleteHelper.java:81), or, once the id is fixed, reports success without removing the codes (see the disableCredentialType finding).

contracts.action: Removal of recovery codes from the account (delete of a federated credential)
contracts.equivalent_path: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/requiredactions/util/CredentialDeleteHelper.java:75-80 (the '-id' placeholder branch, which calls disableCredentialType for the type)
contracts.before_after: Before: recovery codes were never federated, so this path did not apply to them. After: the federated match fails on the null id, and the placeholder branch needs an id ending in '-id', which the codes do not have.
contracts.visible_effect: Today the delete request returns NotFound. Once the id is fixed, it returns success.
contracts.failure_mode: Success is reported while the codes still validate, because disableCredentialType ignores this type.
contracts.open_question: Does the account REST delete endpoint call CredentialDeleteHelper.removeCredential for federated credentials, and does its response depend on the return value?

contracts.action: Login form rendering of the recovery-code prompt (RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean constructor)
contracts.before_after: Before: it read only stored credentials and called .get(). After: it reads federated credentials first, then stored ones, and still calls .get().
contracts.visible_effect: The page asks for the next unused code number, which comes from the federated model when one exists.
contracts.failure_mode: If neither store has a credential, .get() throws NoSuchElementException. This matches the previous behaviour.

contracts.action: Browser-flow selection of the recovery-code authenticator (configuredFor)
contracts.before_after: Before: the provider returned false for this type. After: it returns true when recoveryCodes is set, so the recovery alternative is offered.
contracts.visible_effect: The recovery-code prompt is offered to a federated user who has codes.
contracts.failure_mode: The prompt is offered even though the codes are replayable (see the replay finding).

summary: Setup and login of recovery codes through user storage work at the level the new test covers, but the single-use guarantee and revocation do not hold for user-stored codes. The main problems are: (1) user-storage codes are never consumed, so they can be replayed (test provider, BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340); (2) regenerating codes through user storage does not revoke previously issued local codes (CredentialHelper.java:125-130); (3) raw codes are written to user storage in plaintext (CredentialHelper.java:119). Removal paths are also broken or silent: the returned credential has no id (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:237), and disableCredentialType ignores this type (line 217). The new test covers only the happy path. No docs/adr directory exists at the head commit, so no ADR was checked. Nothing was built or run.
